name: Texas
$scopeNote: Texas has NO state individual wage income tax -- a constitutional prohibition (Tex. Const. Art. VIII, sec. 24, added by voter referendum in 2019) requiring a statewide voter referendum before one could ever be enacted, not a mere policy choice. Never has had one.
exemptPretaxComment: Not applicable -- no income tax exists for any pretax category to reduce the base of.

reciprocity.note: Not applicable -- Texas has no income tax to be reciprocal about, same convention as this project's other no-income-tax states (SD, TN, FL).

localIncomeTax.rule: NONE. No Texas city or county levies a local income/wage tax.

paidFamilyMedicalLeave.rule: NONE mandatory. Texas has no state-run paid family/medical leave program and no state paid-sick-leave mandate. Texas Insurance Code Chapter 1255 (enacted 2023) authorizes licensed private carriers to offer VOLUNTARY group paid-family-leave insurance to employers on an opt-in basis -- no state fund, no mandatory deduction, same voluntary-insurance-only shape as several other states in this project. Additionally, and more forcefully than most other 'no local mandate' states here: the Texas Regulatory Consistency Act (H.B. 2127) affirmatively PREEMPTS cities/counties from creating their own paid-leave or paid-sick-leave ordinances at all, and this preemption has already been enforced in court against real municipal ordinances (Austin, Dallas, San Antonio).

$yearNote: 2025 ruleset, built 2026-09-28 for prior-year corrections and retro pay. Only the fields the engine computes from were re-sourced for 2025 (suiEmployer). Descriptive fields (localIncomeTax.rule, reciprocity, paid-leave notes) are carried from the 2026 file; none of them changed between the two years.

knownGaps: Carried-over descriptive notes aside, this 2025 file models only employer unemployment (and, where the state has them, the employee unemployment, paid-leave, long-term-care and Seattle payroll-expense lines). Anything the 2026 file lists as unmodelled is unmodelled here too.
